snippet_full.title: NEWLY PREGNANT? 10 THINGS Expecting Moms Should Do For A Healthy Start!
snippet_full.description:
Ok once you see those two lines WHAT IN THE WORLD are you supposed to do next?

There's lots to think about including who to tell, when to tell them, what do do about work, what to eat, what to avoid, finding a provider, figuring out a list of questions a first time mom might want to ask their provider....

I will go over lots of this information and more including the differences between a Midwife, an Obstetrician-Gynecologist and a family doctor with experience in obstetrics and when you should be making your first prenatal appointment with them (HINT - its NOW!)

If it's your first pregnancy or you have 6 kiddos already at home watch this video and cruise through this list of 10 THINGS you should do once you find out you're pregnant!

what to do after a positive pregnancy test, first trimester tips, pregnancy care checklist, choosing a prenatal care provider, prenatal vitamins explained

videos_scanned.title: Why it’s so important to rest after birth ? #shorts #postpartumrecovery #postpartum

snippet_full.title: Why it’s so important to rest after birth ? #shorts #postpartumrecovery #postpartum
snippet_full.description:
After 9 long months of pregnancy, most women are eager to jump back into their old fitness routine to get their pre-pregnancy body back. However, after your delivery, you are told to get good rest for 6-8 weeks - here is the reason for that 

Your placenta has an average diameter of 21-22cm that implants on your uterine wall. Once you birth the placenta you are left with a large wound. 

If we saw this wound on the outside we would be in bed resting, we would have people doing everything for us, no one would let you over do it. Yet when you give birth it’s expected of you to rest but also still manage everything else.

Lets be honest this actually leaves little time to rest. 

It takes on average 4-6 weeks for this wound to fully heal. During this time your bleeding, your feeling sore and things feel really different. Not only have you given birth to your baby, but you have also birthed an organ. 

Your body is amazing at healing but it also needs your help to

🔸️Nourish 
🔸️Rest 
🔸️Support

When these three things are set up, women may experience a quicker healing time and feel better much faster. 

Even if your birth was straight forward, this wound like all wounds can reopen, bleed and be susceptible to infection when your overdoing it or not prioritising rest and recovery.

Your body is doing so much during this healing time. 

Do yourself a favour and REST!

#pregnancytips #postpartumhealth

Being pregnant with my 6th baby in 8 years, here is what I pack in my hospital bag each time for a more comfortable stay! Now these are just my personal preference, I would love to hear yours! 

1) Going home outfit for you and baby
2) Toiletries (see below for what I pack in my toiletries bag)
3) Phone charger (pro tip, get a 10ft charging cable)
4) Stroller fan (this can wrap around the hospital bed)
5) Nightlight
6) Ear plugs
7) Sleep mask
8) White noise machine 
9) Pacifiers
10) Pajamas
11) A Nursing bra you can sleep in
12) Your own labor and postpartum gowns if you prefer
13) Cute swaddle and or outfit for baby for hospital pics

Toiletries ⬇️

• lip balm
• lotion
• hair ties
• shampoo 
• conditioner
• body wash
• toothbrush
• toothpaste
• floss
• face wash 
• skincare must haves
• make up

Now these are just my personal preferences, I would love to hear yours! I know many people like to bring their own towel as the one at the hospital is small but I don’t mind it! I know people also like to bring their own pillows but again the hospital ones to bother me!
